title: MakeMyTrip Returns to Profit as Domestic Travel Offsets Weak Rupee
excerpt: The Nasdaq-listed travel company posted a $1.8 million profit in Q2 FY27 on revenue of $235.2 million, with bus ticketing and hotels offsetting subdued international long-haul demand and a roughly 10% rupee depreciation.
body:
• MakeMyTrip swung to a net profit of $1.8 million in Q2 FY27, for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, from a loss of $5.7 million a year earlier.
  • Revenue rose 2.5% to $235.2 million, but grew 11.2% in constant currency — the rupee fell about 10% against the dollar year on year, depressing reported dollar revenue.
  • Gross bookings rose to $2.72 billion, up 11.3% reported and 20.9% in constant currency, led by bus ticketing revenue up 16.6% to $39.1 million.
  • For investors, the quarter underlines the split in the business: domestic hotels and ground transport are growing in double digits in constant currency, while international long-haul remains exposed to fuel-driven airfares and the rupee — track NASDAQ: MMYT through the company's investor relations page.

A return to profit, held back by currency

Nasdaq-listed MakeMyTrip reported a consolidated net profit of $1.8 million for the second quarter of fiscal 2027, reversing a $5.7 million loss in the same quarter last year, according to Inc42 and the company's results coverage. Revenue increased 2.5% year on year to $235.2 million from $229.3 million.

The headline growth rate understates the underlying business. On a constant-currency basis, revenue grew 11.2% to $255.0 million, VieStories reported from the company's results. MakeMyTrip reports in dollars while the functional currency of its major subsidiaries is the rupee, and the rupee depreciated approximately 10% against the dollar compared with the year-ago quarter.

Profitability improved on several measures. Operating profit rose 6.5% to $36.7 million, adjusted operating profit rose 4.7% to $46.2 million and adjusted EBITDA rose 6.4% to $51.5 million. Net finance costs fell to $29.8 million from $35.9 million, helped by lower net foreign-exchange losses, and diluted earnings per share improved to $0.02 from a loss of $0.06.

"Growth in hotels and ground transport underscored the resilience of our diversified portfolio and our ability to serve evolving customer needs."

— Rajesh Magow, Group CEO, MakeMyTrip

Where the growth came from

Gross bookings increased to $2.72 billion. Hotels and packages remained the largest revenue contributor at $107.1 million, down 1% in reported terms but up 7.4% in constant currency, with hotel room nights up 18.5% and adjusted margin up 10.4% to $116.8 million.

Bus ticketing was the fastest-growing major segment. Revenue climbed 16.6% to $39.1 million, or 25.7% in constant currency, as the number of bus tickets sold rose 24.7% and segment gross bookings rose 20% to $435.3 million. Revenue from other businesses, including ancillary services and car bookings, rose 21.6% to $32.3 million.

Air ticketing moved the other way in reported terms. Revenue fell 7.2% to $56.7 million, though it rose 0.6% in constant currency, and its adjusted margin as a share of gross bookings eased to 6.9% from 7.2%.

Why outbound travel stayed subdued

International long-haul outbound travel from India remained subdued, the company said. Elevated fuel prices pushed up airfares, and the weaker rupee raised the overall cost of overseas trips, while strong domestic travel demand partially offset those pressures.

Group CEO Rajesh Magow said the company had "delivered strong growth despite a challenging travel environment," according to PhocusWire, and pointed to the use of artificial intelligence to simplify planning and booking.

Balance sheet and what to watch

MakeMyTrip generated free cash flow of $47.1 million in the quarter, up 3.2%, though first-half free cash flow fell 19.8% to $67.1 million. At September 30 it held $427.9 million in cash and cash equivalents including restricted cash, plus $388.6 million in term deposits. It repurchased 345,158 ordinary shares for $17.2 million in the quarter, leaving $78.6 million of repurchase authorisation.

The test for coming quarters is conversion: whether 20.9% constant-currency growth in gross bookings translates into faster reported revenue and sustained net profit if the rupee and fuel prices stay unfavourable. Domestic demand is carrying the business for now.
